ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Answer-likelihood gain as a reward for every search turn
PROPOSAL: Train a search agent on question-answer pairs from NQ and HotpotQA with a group-based policy gradient. After each turn, measure the log probability that the current policy assigns to the ground-truth answer given the trajectory so far, and reward the change from the previous turn. Normalise the change within the group, then add it to the outcome reward with a fixed weight. Turns that bring in useful evidence raise the answer likelihood and turns that distract lower it, so rollouts with the same final answer still receive different advantages. Evaluate exact match on seven question-answering benchmarks with a three-billion-parameter base model.
CONTROLS: Compare against outcome-only training with the same rollouts per query. Compare against turn rewards shuffled across the turns of each trajectory. Hold the retriever, the base model and the update count fixed, and repeat each run with three seeds.
COST: 210
PREDICTION: Exact match should rise over outcome-only training, most on multi-hop benchmarks, and the share of groups with zero advantage should fall. The idea fails if shuffled turn rewards give the same exact match.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evidence-hit reward from gold answer strings in tool responses
PROPOSAL: Give each turn of a search rollout a reward that equals one when the tool response contains the ground-truth answer string or a listed alias and the answer was absent from every earlier response, and zero otherwise. This needs only the question and its final answer, with no step labels, external judge or tree search. Add the reward to the outcome reward after normalising inside the group, and cap the total from turn rewards so the agent cannot gain more by retrieving than by answering correctly. Train a seven-billion-parameter base model on a mix of single-hop and multi-hop questions, and measure exact match, retrieval hit rate and the number of turns per answer.
CONTROLS: Compare against outcome-only training, against a reward for any new document regardless of its content, and against turn rewards that ignore the cap. Keep the retriever and the data order fixed and use three seeds.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Training with the evidence-hit reward should improve exact match on multi-hop questions and lift retrieval hit rate. It fails if the any-new-document reward matches it, because then the answer string adds no information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Matched-rollout comparison of sample efficiency for turn-level rewards
PROPOSAL: Measure whether turn-level supervision gives better accuracy for fewer sampled trajectories. Train a three-billion-parameter agent with outcome-only group training and with an added turn-level information term, logging exact match on a fixed validation set after every block of one hundred queries. Count the total rollouts and tool calls consumed, and plot exact match against rollouts consumed. Fit the area under each curve and the rollouts needed to reach a target accuracy. Use NQ, HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA for training and the remaining benchmarks for testing, so that the gain is checked on questions the agent never trained on.
CONTROLS: The reference run is outcome-only training with the same group size and optimiser. Add a run with double the rollouts per query to separate sample efficiency from raw data volume. Repeat all runs with five seeds and report spread, since curves from a single seed can cross by chance.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The turn-level run should reach the target accuracy with clearly fewer rollouts than outcome-only training, and not merely match the doubled-rollout run. The claim fails if the curves overlap within seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Using turn rewards to break ties when all rollouts share an outcome
PROPOSAL: Detect groups in which every rollout has the same outcome reward, which would otherwise yield zero advantage, and in those groups switch on a turn-level signal. The signal compares the number of turns that retrieve a document containing the ground-truth answer, so successful trajectories that find the answer earlier and failed trajectories that come closer receive different advantages. Groups with mixed outcomes keep the usual outcome advantage. Train a small base model on question-answer pairs from HotpotQA and Musique, where hard questions often yield all-wrong groups, and record the share of groups that produce a gradient.
CONTROLS: Compare against outcome-only training, against always adding the turn signal, and against breaking ties with random noise. Keep rollouts per query, optimiser and data order fixed, and repeat with three seeds.
COST: 330
PREDICTION: The share of groups with a gradient should rise sharply and accuracy on hard multi-hop questions should improve over outcome-only training. The idea fails if noise tie-breaking gives the same accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Difficulty-aware query sampling combined with turn-level rewards
PROPOSAL: Estimate the success rate of each training question from its recent rollouts, then sample more questions with success rates between the extremes, where groups carry gradient. Combine this sampler with a dense reward on each turn that tracks the rise in ground-truth answer likelihood. Train a two-billion-parameter model on NQ, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Musique, and compare accuracy and the share of groups with a nonzero advantage. The sampler uses only the questions and final answers, so it needs no external judge or step annotation, and it adds a small bookkeeping cost to each update.
CONTROLS: Compare against uniform sampling with turn rewards, against the sampler alone with outcome rewards, and against outcome-only training with uniform sampling. Fix rollouts per query and the update count, and use three seeds.
COST: 95
PREDICTION: Combined training should yield the highest exact match, and each component alone should recover part of the gain. It fails if the sampler alone matches the combination.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Auditing turn rewards for drift away from the final objective
PROPOSAL: Check whether the dense reward invites reward hacking. Train a search agent with an answer-likelihood turn reward, and track the correlation between summed turn reward and final correctness during training. Build adversarial probes: give the agent questions where repeating the same search query raises the likelihood of a wrong answer, and questions where a tool response contains a distractor answer. Count how often the agent exploits them. If the correlation falls or exploitation rises, lower the turn weight and rerun. Use a three-billion-parameter model on HotpotQA and report exact match with the audit results.
CONTROLS: Compare the turn reward weight at three values against outcome-only training. Include a probe set where the correct behaviour is known, and keep the retriever fixed.
COST: 180
PREDICTION: Correlation between turn reward and final correctness should stay high and exploitation of the probes should stay low at moderate weights. The audit fails if exploitation grows with training time even at small weights.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn-level rewards for weaker search agents
PROPOSAL: Test the claim that weaker models gain most from turn-level supervision. Train base models of one, three and seven billion parameters with outcome-only group training and with an added turn reward based on answer likelihood. For each size record exact match on HotpotQA, Musique and Bamboogle, and the share of groups that give zero advantage. Plot the gain from the turn reward against model size. Weaker models should have more uniformly wrong groups, so the turn reward should help them most. Use the same search tool, the same retriever and the same data for all runs.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only training for each size. Add a run that gives the small model extra outcome-only updates matched to the extra compute of the turn reward. Repeat with three seeds.
COST: 1100
PREDICTION: The gain from turn rewards should shrink as model size grows, and the zero-advantage share should be highest for the smallest model. The claim fails if gains are flat across sizes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Corrupted-prefix tests of turn-level credit assignment
PROPOSAL: Train an agent with a turn-level information reward, then test credit assignment directly. Take successful trajectories, replace one turn with a poor query or an off-topic tool response, and compute the turn rewards that follow. A good credit assignment rule gives low reward to the corrupted turn and shows how later turns lose or keep their value. Compare the drop in reward at the corrupted turn with the drop at turns left intact, over two hundred HotpotQA trajectories. Report the rank correlation between turn reward and an oracle label for the corrupted turn.
CONTROLS: Compare against outcome-only credit, where every turn shares the final reward, and against uniform random turn scores. Repeat with three seeds and several corruption positions.
COST: 45
PREDICTION: Corrupted turns should receive clearly lower reward than intact ones, with a positive rank correlation. The test fails if the turn reward cannot distinguish corrupted from intact turns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-turn discounting of information-gain rewards in long trajectories
PROPOSAL: Study how the credit given to early turns changes with a discount on later gains. Define the turn reward as the discounted sum of future likelihood increases for the ground-truth answer, so an early query that sets up later success keeps credit. Train a three-billion-parameter agent on multi-hop questions with discount factors from zero to one, and record exact match, mean number of turns and the share of groups with a gradient. Longer chains need larger discounts, so inspect results separately for two-hop and four-hop questions.
CONTROLS: Compare against outcome-only training and against the undiscounted single-turn gain. Fix the retriever and optimiser and repeat each factor with three seeds.
COST: 560
PREDICTION: An intermediate discount should give the highest exact match on the longest chains. The idea fails if every factor performs within seed spread of the undiscounted gain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of turn-level reward training to unseen question distributions
PROPOSAL: Train on NQ and HotpotQA only, then evaluate on benchmarks the agent never saw: 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique, Bamboogle, TriviaQA and PopQA. Use outcome-only group training and the same training with a turn-level answer-likelihood reward, with the same base model, search tool and rollouts. Report exact match per benchmark and the average. Test whether the turn reward helps on distributions with different question styles and longer reasoning chains, and whether the agent becomes more reliable on questions where retrieval often fails.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only training on the same data. Add a run trained on all benchmarks to show the gap that distribution shift leaves. Repeat with three seeds.
COST: 4200
PREDICTION: Turn-level training should raise average exact match on unseen benchmarks, most on multi-hop sets. The claim fails if the gain appears only on the training distributions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Information-gain turn rewards for group-based search agent training
PROPOSAL: Train a search agent on question-answer pairs from NQ and HotpotQA with group-based policy updates. After each turn compute the rise in the log probability of the ground-truth answer, conditioned on the trajectory so far, and add this normalised gain to the outcome reward as a per-turn term. The study checks whether rollouts that share an identical outcome still differ in their turn rewards, giving nonzero advantages. Evaluate exact match on seven question-answering benchmarks with a three-billion-parameter base model, using the same search tool and retriever for all runs.
CONTROLS: Compare against outcome-only group training with the same rollouts per query. Compare against turn rewards assigned in a permuted order across the turns of each trajectory. Hold the retriever, the base model and the update count fixed across runs. Repeat each run over several seeds and report the spread.
COST: 210
PREDICTION: Exact match should rise over outcome-only training, most on multi-hop benchmarks. The idea fails if permuted turn rewards reach the same exact match, since the gain then does not depend on credit order.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Format-validity turn rewards for group-based search agent training
PROPOSAL: Fit a search agent on question-answer pairs drawn from NQ and HotpotQA using group-based policy updates. Once a turn finishes, test whether the tool call parses and whether the reasoning tags close, then blend the resulting score into the outcome reward as a per-turn term. Rollouts that end in an identical outcome thus still receive distinct turn rewards, producing nonzero advantages. Report exact match across seven question-answering benchmarks with a three-billion-parameter base model, keeping the search tool and retriever identical in every run.
CONTROLS: Contrast with a prompt-only workflow driven by the same search tool and retriever. Contrast with turn rewards handed out in reversed order within each trajectory. Hold the retriever, the base model and the update count fixed across runs. Repeat each run over several seeds and report the spread.
COST: 210
PREDICTION: Exact match should rise over the prompt-only workflow, most on multi-hop benchmarks. The idea fails if reversed turn rewards reach the same exact match, since the gain then does not depend on turn order.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evidence-recall turn rewards with a cap against reward drift
PROPOSAL: Grant each turn of a rollout a reward the first time the tool response holds the ground-truth answer string or a listed alias. Fold the reward into the outcome reward after normalising inside the group, and cap what turn rewards can contribute in total, so retrieval never pays more than a correct answer. Fit a seven-billion-parameter base model on a mix of single-hop and multi-hop questions from NQ, HotpotQA and Musique, and measure exact match, retrieval recall and turns per answer.
CONTROLS: Contrast with outcome-only training, and with a reward for any new document regardless of its content. Contrast cap values by running the cap at its tuned value and with the cap removed, with data order held fixed. Repeat each run over several seeds and report the spread.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Evidence-recall training should lift exact match on multi-hop questions and keep turns per answer stable. It fails if the any-new-document reward reaches the same exact match, since the answer string then adds little information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Document-novelty turn rewards with a cap against reward drift
PROPOSAL: Score every step of a rollout once a retrieved page shows up that the trajectory has not yet seen. Combine the score with the outcome reward after normalising inside the group, and limit the total that step scores can contribute, so retrieval cannot outweigh a correct answer. Run a seven-billion-parameter base model on a mix of single-hop and multi-hop questions from NQ, HotpotQA and Musique, and tabulate exact match, page count and turns per answer.
CONTROLS: Compare against outcome-only training, and against credit for any query whatever it says. Compare limit values by running the limit at its tuned value and with the limit lifted, with data order held fixed. Repeat each run over several seeds and report the spread.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Novelty training should lift the page count and keep turns per answer stable. It fails if the any-query credit reaches the same page count, since the novelty test then adds little information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn-level supervision on multi-hop questions with uniformly wrong groups
PROPOSAL: Train a three-billion-parameter search agent on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Musique, keeping the hard questions on which most rollout groups end uniformly wrong. Add an answer-likelihood term to every turn, and measure the share of groups with a nonzero advantage together with exact match. The study asks whether turn rewards restore a gradient where outcome rewards leave it flat. Run training until the policy settles, with eight rollouts per query, and test on held-out questions of the same hard type.
CONTROLS: Compare against outcome-only training on the same hard questions with the same rollouts per query. Compare against turn rewards on easy questions, where groups are mixed already. Vary the group size across a short list while the rest stays fixed. Repeat each run over several seeds and report the spread.
COST: 1350
PREDICTION: The share of groups with a nonzero advantage should be far higher with turn rewards on the hard questions, and exact match should rise. It fails if outcome-only training already yields a gradient on most groups.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn-level supervision on single-hop questions with mixed groups
PROPOSAL: Fit a three-billion-parameter search agent on NQ, TriviaQA and PopQA, selecting easy questions whose rollout groups mostly come out mixed. Attach an answer-likelihood bonus to each turn, and record the fraction of groups with a nonzero advantage next to exact match. The study asks whether turn rewards keep a gradient alive where outcome rewards already supply one. Continue training until the policy stabilises, using eight rollouts per query, and score unseen questions of the same easy type.
CONTROLS: Contrast with outcome-only training on those easy questions at the same rollouts per query. Contrast with turn rewards on hard questions, where most groups end wrong already. Vary the group size across a short list while the rest stays fixed. Repeat each run over several seeds and report the spread.
COST: 1350
PREDICTION: The fraction of groups with a nonzero advantage should be close with turn rewards on the easy questions, and exact match should rise slightly. It fails if outcome-only training yields a gradient on fewer groups.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Checking that turn rewards track the progress of the search, not its length
PROPOSAL: Test the credibility of a turn-level reward on trajectories from a trained search agent. For each turn compute the rise in the log probability of the ground-truth answer, then relate it to an oracle label of whether the turn retrieved a supporting passage, available for a small HotpotQA subset. Report the rank correlation between turn reward and the oracle label, and the area under the curve for separating supporting from non-supporting turns. This tests whether the reward tracks progress toward the answer.
CONTROLS: Contrast the turn reward with the oracle label on the same trajectories. Contrast with the position of the turn in the trajectory, which a length effect follows. Hold the retriever and the question set fixed, and vary the trajectory length. Repeat the scoring on a second sample of questions.
COST: 58
PREDICTION: The turn reward should correlate with the oracle label far better than turn position does. The check fails if position explains as much of the reward as the label.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Checking that token counts track the cost of the search, not its progress
PROPOSAL: Examine a turn-level quantity on trajectories sampled from a trained search agent. At each turn count the tokens in the tool response, then relate the count to a timing label saying whether the turn finished quickly, available for a small HotpotQA subset. Give the rank correlation between token count and timing label, plus the area under the curve for telling fast turns from slow ones. This examines whether the count follows the size of the response.
CONTROLS: Compare the token count against the timing label on the same trajectories. Compare against the position of the turn in the trajectory, which a length effect follows. Hold the retriever and the question set fixed, and vary the trajectory length. Repeat the scoring on a second sample of questions.
COST: 58
PREDICTION: The token count should correlate with the timing label far better than turn position does. The check fails if position explains as much of the count as the label.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample efficiency of turn-level rewards against outcome-only training
PROPOSAL: Train a three-billion-parameter agent on NQ, HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA with outcome-only group training and with an added turn-level information term. Log exact match on a fixed validation set after every block of queries, and record the total rollouts and tool calls consumed. Plot exact match against rollouts consumed, and read off the rollouts needed to reach a target accuracy. Evaluate on Musique, Bamboogle and TriviaQA, kept out of training.
CONTROLS: Compare each method at the same number of rollouts consumed, not at the same number of updates. Compare against outcome-only training given extra rollouts per query, to match the data volume of the turn-level run. Hold the optimiser and the validation set fixed. Repeat all runs over several seeds and report the spread.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The turn-level run should reach the target accuracy with fewer rollouts than outcome-only training, and not merely match the run with extra rollouts. The claim fails if the curves overlap within the spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Wall-clock speed of turn-level rewards against outcome-only training
PROPOSAL: Fit a three-billion-parameter agent over NQ, HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA with outcome-only group training and again with an added turn-level information term. Log exact match on a fixed validation set after each block of queries, and tally the seconds elapsed and tool calls issued. Chart exact match against seconds elapsed, and read off the seconds required to hit a target accuracy. Test on Musique, Bamboogle and TriviaQA, which the agent never trained on.
CONTROLS: Contrast the methods at one shared count of seconds elapsed, not at one shared count of updates. Contrast with outcome-only training given extra workers per query, to mirror the machine load of the turn-level run. Hold the optimiser and the validation questions fixed. Repeat every run over several seeds and give the spread.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The turn-level run should reach the target accuracy in fewer seconds than outcome-only training, and not merely match the run with extra workers. The claim fails if the curves overlap within the spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Answer-likelihood turn rewards from questions and final answers alone
PROPOSAL: Reward each interaction turn by the rise in the log probability of the ground-truth answer given the trajectory so far, computed by the policy itself. The signal uses the question and the final answer already in the training data, with no step labels, external judge or tree search. Normalise the turn reward inside the group and add it to the outcome reward. Train a three-billion-parameter base model on NQ and HotpotQA and evaluate exact match on seven benchmarks.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only group training with the same rollouts per query. Runs are repeated with several seeds, and the data order is held fixed.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: Exact match should rise over outcome-only training, most on multi-hop benchmarks. The direction fails if turn rewards leave the share of zero-advantage groups unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gold-evidence matching turn rewards from annotated supporting passages
PROPOSAL: Reward each interaction turn by the overlap between the retrieved passage and the gold supporting passage, scored by an annotator-written list for the question. The signal uses the supporting passages that annotators wrote for HotpotQA and Musique, with a trained relevance model to score unseen retrievals. Normalise the turn reward inside the group and add it to the outcome reward. Train a three-billion-parameter base model on NQ and HotpotQA and evaluate exact match on seven benchmarks.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only group training with the same rollouts per query. Runs are repeated with several seeds, and the data order is held fixed.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: Exact match should rise over outcome-only training, most on multi-hop benchmarks. The direction fails if turn rewards leave the share of unsupported passages unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn signals that restore gradients when a whole group agrees
PROPOSAL: Detect groups in which every rollout shares one outcome reward, and in those groups add a turn-level signal that compares how early each trajectory retrieves a passage containing the ground-truth answer. Mixed groups keep the usual outcome advantage. Train a small base model on HotpotQA and Musique, where hard questions often give uniformly wrong groups, and record the share of groups that produce a gradient and the exact match.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only group training. Runs share the optimiser and data order and are repeated with several seeds.
COST: 75
PREDICTION: The share of groups with a gradient should rise and accuracy on hard questions should improve. The direction fails if the share stays at the outcome-only level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Larger groups and higher temperature to avoid agreeing outcomes
PROPOSAL: Detect questions on which every rollout shares one outcome reward, and for those questions enlarge the group and raise the sampling temperature so more rollouts differ. Mixed groups keep the usual group size. Train a small base model on HotpotQA and Musique, where hard questions often give uniformly wrong groups, and record the share of groups that differ in outcome and the exact match.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only group training. Runs share the optimiser and data order and are repeated with several seeds.
COST: 75
PREDICTION: The share of groups with differing outcomes should rise and diversity of queries should improve. The direction fails if the share stays at the standard level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rollout budget curves for turn-level supervision on multi-hop search
PROPOSAL: Measure whether turn-level supervision turns each sampled trajectory into more learning. Train a three-billion-parameter agent with outcome-only group training and with an added information-gain turn term, and log exact match on a fixed validation set as the number of consumed rollouts grows. Fit the area under each curve and the rollouts needed to reach a target accuracy. Train on NQ and HotpotQA and test on Musique, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Bamboogle.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only training with the same group size and optimiser. Runs are repeated with several seeds, and curves are drawn against rollouts consumed.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The turn-level run should reach the target accuracy with fewer rollouts than outcome-only training. The direction fails if the curves overlap within seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training throughput curves for turn-level supervision on multi-hop search
PROPOSAL: Check whether turn-level supervision turns each training step into more updates per second. Train a three-billion-parameter agent with outcome-only group training and with an added information-gain turn term, and log tokens processed per second as the number of workers grows. Compute the area under each curve and the workers needed to reach a target throughput. Use NQ and HotpotQA for training and Musique, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Bamboogle for testing.
CONTROLS: The reference is plain outcome training at the same group size with the usual optimiser. Seeds are repeated several times, and curves are drawn against workers used.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The turn-level run should reach the target throughput with fewer workers than outcome-only training. The direction fails if the curves overlap within seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probing turn rewards for exploitation by repeated or distracting queries
PROPOSAL: Check whether dense turn rewards invite reward hacking. Train a search agent with an answer-likelihood turn term, and track the correlation between summed turn reward and final correctness. Build probes: questions where repeating a query raises the likelihood of a wrong answer, and tool responses that contain a distractor answer. Count how often the agent exploits them, and lower the turn weight if exploitation rises. Use a three-billion-parameter model on HotpotQA.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only training on the same questions. Weights are tried at a short list of values, and runs are repeated with several seeds.
COST: 340
PREDICTION: The correlation should stay high and exploitation of the probes should stay low at moderate weights. The direction fails if exploitation grows with training even at small weights.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Probing outcome rewards for format errors under repeated or lengthy queries
PROPOSAL: Examine whether exact-match outcome rewards invite parsing failures. Train a search agent with an exact-match outcome term, and follow the correlation between tool-call count and parse errors. Prepare probes: questions where a repeated query lengthens the response, and tool responses holding a long distractor passage. Tally how often the agent breaks the format, and shorten the length limit if breaks rise. Use a three-billion-parameter model on HotpotQA.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only training on the same questions. Limits are tried at a short list of values, and runs are repeated with several seeds.
COST: 340
PREDICTION: Format breaks should stay low and the correlation with tool-call count should stay high at moderate limits. The direction fails if breaks grow with training even at small limits.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Corrupted-prefix tests of turn-level credit assignment
PROPOSAL: Take successful search trajectories from a trained agent and replace one turn with a poor query or an off-topic tool response. Compute the turn rewards of the corrupted trajectory from the rise in ground-truth answer likelihood, and compare the reward at the corrupted turn with the reward at intact turns, over two hundred HotpotQA trajectories. A sound credit rule gives the corrupted turn low reward. Report the rank correlation between turn reward and an oracle label of the corrupted turn.
CONTROLS: The reference is outcome-only credit, where every turn shares the final reward. Corruption positions are varied, and runs are repeated with several seeds.
COST: 28
PREDICTION: Corrupted turns should receive clearly lower reward than intact ones. The direction fails if turn rewards cannot separate corrupted from intact turns.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prompt-length tests of reasoning effort in search trajectories
PROPOSAL: Take successful search trajectories from a trained agent and lengthen one reasoning step with filler text or an added instruction. Compute the answer accuracy of the lengthened trajectory from the final exact match, and compare the accuracy at the lengthened turn with the accuracy at unchanged turns, over two hundred HotpotQA trajectories. A sound reasoning rule gives the lengthened turn higher accuracy. Report the rank correlation between step length and an oracle label of the lengthened turn.
CONTROLS: The reference is the unchanged prompt, where every step keeps its original length. Lengthening positions are varied, and runs are repeated with several seeds.
COST: 28
PREDICTION: Lengthened turns should receive clearly higher accuracy than unchanged ones. The direction fails if step length cannot separate lengthened from unchanged turns.
